title: ColumnDisturb: Understanding Column-based Read Disturbance in Real DRAM Chips and Implications for Future Systems
problem: A newly discovered DRAM read disturbance phenomenon called ColumnDisturb allows a single aggressor row activation to disturb DRAM cells through bitlines (columns), inducing bitflips in rows sharing the same columns across multiple subarrays — up to 3072 rows simultaneously in DDR4 — which is fundamentally different from RowHammer/RowPress that affect only a few adjacent rows in a single subarray.
motivation: As DRAM technology scales to smaller nodes, ColumnDisturb worsens (first-bitflip time reduces by up to 5.06x), threatening both the correctness of existing DRAM chips and the performance/energy benefits of retention-aware refresh mechanisms that are being proposed to improve DRAM efficiency.
method: The researchers tested 216 DDR4 chips and 4 HBM2 chips from three major manufacturers, systematically varying temperature, data patterns, and memory timing parameters (tRCD, tRAS, tRP—specific delays between memory operations) to trigger bitflips (bit errors). They measured how quickly the first bitflip occurred and how many rows were affected under normal 63.6-millisecond refresh intervals (the time window when memory refreshes stored data). By simulating the detailed circuit behavior and comparing against normal data-loss rates, they demonstrated how this disturbance could undermine power-saving strategies that skip refreshes for cells known to retain data reliably.
key_novelty: This is the first detailed experimental study of ColumnDisturb, a disturbance where a single activated memory row can damage cells across up to 3 subarrays (sections of a chip) through shared electrical paths (bitlines/columns), affecting far more rows at once than RowHammer.
contributions: First experimental demonstration of ColumnDisturb on 216 DDR4 and 4 HBM2 chips from three manufacturers, with 27 key characterization findings
Quantification that ColumnDisturb worsens with DRAM technology scaling and occurs within nominal DDR4 refresh windows on real chips
Analysis showing ColumnDisturb induces bitflips in up to 198x more rows than retention failures, severely undermining retention-aware refresh mechanism benefits
Evaluation of two mitigation solutions and a call for further research into column-based DRAM disturbance

metrics.other: First-bitflip time reduces by up to 5.06x (2.96x average) with smaller DRAM node; affects up to 3072 rows simultaneously; induces bitflips within 63.6ms DDR4 refresh window on real chips; up to 198x more affected rows than retention failures

limitations: The paper characterizes the phenomenon and evaluates two mitigations but does not fully specify or evaluate a complete production-ready mitigation solution; HBM2 characterization covers only 4 chips.
primary_theme: New DRAM column-based read disturbance phenomenon characterization
